title: fix(core): restore AST fidelity for headings, titles and reference links
body:
## Summary / 摘要 Fix three fidelity defects in the Lezer→mdast adapter that silently dropped heading text, link/image titles, and reference-link destinations from `editor.getAst()`. 修复 Lezer→mdast adapter 的三处保真度缺陷：标题文字、link/image 的 title、 以及引用式链接的目标地址在 `editor.getAst()` 中被静默丢弃。 ## Motivation / 背景与动机 `lezerStringToMdast` is the single chokepoint every AST consumer reads through — the outline, word count, `exportHTML()`, and any plugin calling `getAst()`. Three things it produced did not match what `remark-parse` produces for the same source, so the loss was invisible in the editor and surfaced only downstream. **1. Setext and closed ATX headings lost all their text.** `headingTextRange` was written for one heading shape: skip the leading `HeaderMark` run, then trim a trailing one. Both CommonMark heading forms use the same `HeaderMark` node name, so that walk misreads the other two layouts: | source | Lezer children | old result | |---|---|---| | `# Title` | `HeaderMark` | correct | | `Title\n=====` | `HeaderMark` (the underline, **after** the text) | `children: []` | | `## Title ##` | `HeaderMark`, `HeaderMark` (adjacent siblings) | `children: []` | For setext the sole mark is the underline, so it was skipped as the opening mark *and* trimmed as the closing mark, leaving `cursor` past `end`. For closed ATX, Lezer keeps the heading text in raw source rather than a child node, so the two marks are immediate siblings and the leading `while` consumed both. Either way `depth` and `position` stayed correct while `children` came out empty. That is why it went unnoticed: the editor's live-preview decoration reads the syntax tree directly and looked fine, while AST consumers broke — - outline entries rendered as clickable buttons with **no accessible name** (WCAG 4.1.2), since `outline-panel.ts` sets `textContent` from `entry.text` - `plugin-wordcount` under-counted (a 15-word document reported 5) - `exportHTML()` emitted `

` `lezer-helpers.ts` already maps `SetextHeading1`/`SetextHeading2` to a depth, so setext was meant to work — this is a regression in the text path, not a missing feature. **2. `title` was hardcoded to `null`** on every Link and Image, though Lezer exposes it as a `LinkTitle` child. `live-preview-table.ts` already reads `node.title`, so it was reading a value that could never be set. **3. Reference links were emitted as plain links with the raw source as the url.** `[full][ref]` became `{type: "link", url: "[full][ref]"}`, which exports as `` — a dead link. In the editor it also fell through to the GFM bare-URL branch, hiding no brackets and publishing the same string as `data-link-url`. mdast models these as `linkReference`/`imageReference` with the destination left in the companion `definition`; `plugin-wordcount` already handles both node types, which suggests that was always the intended output. - Issue: — - Roadmap (docs/ROADMAP.md): — - OpenSpec change: — (bug fixes only; no new capability, per CONTRIBUTING.md §3.1) ## Changes / 变更内容 - `packages/core`: - `lezer-mdast-adapter.ts` - `headingTextRange`: split the setext and ATX shapes apart instead of sharing one walk, and take a single node at each end rather than looping. - `readLinkTitle`: read the `LinkTitle` child, stripping whichever of the three CommonMark delimiter pairs it carries (`"…"`, `'…'`, `(…)`) and collapsing an empty title to `null` to match remark. - `unwrapUrl`: drop the `<…>` delimiters around a destination — the form exists so a url may contain spaces, and the brackets are not part of it. - `readReference`: classify the three reference forms off the `LinkLabel` child and emit `linkReference` / `imageReference`. - `readLinkLabelChildren`: the existing label walk, extracted from an inline IIFE so references reuse it and keep nested marks (`[**bold**][ref]` stays a `strong`). - `adaptLinkReference`: read the `LinkLabel` / `URL` / `LinkTitle` children instead of re-parsing the line with `/^\[([^\]]+)\]:\s*(\S+)(?:\s+"([^"]*)")?/`, which lost three things the node tree already had right — `\S+` truncated an angle-bracketed url at the first space, only the double-quoted title form matched, and `identifier` kept the author's casing where mdast case-folds it so `[Foo]` resolves against `[foo]: …`. - `types.ts`, `live-preview-ranges.ts`, `live-preview.ts`: changing the node type means the decoration path has to follow, or the editor silently stops rendering reference links. `linkReference` joins the `LivePreviewNode` union and the `isLivePreviewNode` allowlist, and `getInlineMarkerStyle` gains a case that hides the brackets without attaching a url it does not have. - `packages/plugin-*`: — - `apps/electron-demo`: — - `openspec/`: — ### Known deviation from remark Documented on `readReference`: CommonMark only treats `[text][ref]` as a reference when a matching definition exists, and falls back to literal text otherwise. Checking that needs every definition in the document up front, which would turn this adapter's single pass into two — and staying cheap enough for the live-preview hot path is the reason it exists (see the note at the top of the file). So an undefined reference is still emitted as a `linkReference`; consumers that care can check `identifier` against the document's `definition` nodes. Happy to revisit if you'd rather take the second pass. ## Testing / 测试 - [x] `pnpm test` passes / 全绿 — **569 passed / 36 files** (baseline on `main`: 537 / 34). The three commits were verified one at a time, not just the tip: 546 → 558 → 569, no regressions at any step. - [x] Affected packages build (`pnpm build`) / 受影响包构建通过 — `pnpm --filter @floatboat/nexus-core build` (ESM + DTS), and `tsc --noEmit` clean. - [x] New / updated vitest cases / 新增或更新的 vitest 用例： - `test/lezer-mdast-adapter.test.ts` (new, 9) — setext h1/h2 text, inline marks inside a setext heading, setext vs equivalent ATX agreeing, ATX marker stripping, closed ATX (`## Closed ##`, `## Trail #`, `###### Six ######`), `position` spanning the underline, empty setext not throwing. - `test/lezer-mdast-adapter-links.test.ts` (new, 12+11) — the three title delimiter forms, empty title → `null`, whitespace inside a title preserved, title kept out of the label, `<…>` url unwrapping, the three reference forms with case-folded `identifier` and verbatim `label`, nested marks in a reference label, `imageReference` alt text, inline links still plain links, and definition parsing. - `test/live-preview-ranges.test.ts`, `test/live-preview.test.ts` (updated) — reference links stay in the range set under the new node type, their brackets are hidden, and no `data-link-url` is published. - [x] Manual UI check in electron-demo / electron-demo 手动验证： A document with one setext h1, one setext h2, one ATX h1 and one closed ATX h2, opened side by side against `main` (screenshots below). The outline went from a single labelled entry — the other three headings rendered as buttons with no accessible name — to all four labelled and correctly indented, and the word count from `6 words / 15 chars` to `20 words / 46 chars`. Not covered, and deliberately out of scope: in the editor body, setext headings are still not styled as headings, and a closed ATX heading — now correctly recognised as one — still shows its trailing `##`. Both live in the `live-preview.ts` decoration path, a separate concern from AST fidelity, and worth a follow-up PR rather than widening this diff. ## Compliance / 合规自检 - [ ] **CLA signed** — first-time contributors will be prompted automatically by the CLA bot / 首次贡献者按 CLA 机器人提示签署 - [ ] **AI disclosure**: the functional code in this PR is **not** primarily generated by AI. AI assistance, if any, is described below. AI-assisted notes / AI 使用说明: Claude Code was used throughout, including for the functional code. It analysed the adapter and its consumers, proposed candidate defects, and each one was reproduced in a running editor to confirm the behaviour and locate the cause before any code was written. Scope, commit boundaries and the side-by-side verification against an unmodified `main` were my calls; the diagnosis for the closed-ATX case took two attempts, the first being wrong until the Lezer tree was dumped. - [x] **New dependencies** (if any) listed with license & rationale (none if blank): none / 无 - [x] **No build artifacts** committed (`dist/`, `dist-electron/`, compiled `.js` from `.ts`) / 未提交构建产物 - [x] **No secrets** / `.env` / personal vault data committed / 无敏感信息 ## Checklist / 自检清单 - [x] Title follows Conventional Commits / 标题遵循 Conventional Commits - [x] Public API changes update package README / types — 改了公共 API 已同步 README 与类型 — `LivePreviewNode` in `types.ts` gains `LinkReference`. `getAst()` now returns `linkReference` / `imageReference` where it previously returned `link` / `image` for reference syntax; that is the mdast-correct shape, but it is a visible change for anyone switching on `node.type`, so flagging it explicitly. Happy to add a note to the core README if you'd like. - [x] Touched `live-preview-table.ts` → walked through the 12 Table Widget rules in CLAUDE.md / 已核对 12 条表格规则 — not touched (n/a) - [x] New capability / breaking change → OpenSpec proposal linked / 新 capability 或破坏性变更已附 OpenSpec — no new capability; see the API note above - [x] Change aligns with project scope (GOVERNANCE.md §4) / 改动符合 GOVERNANCE.md §4 的项目范围 ## Screenshots / Recordings · 截图或录屏 (UI changes) Same document, same demo, `main` on the left and this branch on the right. **Before** — the outline lists one heading; the two setext headings and the closed ATX heading are missing their labels entirely. **After** — all four headings labelled and indented by depth; word count corrected from 6 to 20.

commits_at_first_review.message:
fix(core): keep heading text for setext and closed ATX headings `headingTextRange` was written for the ATX shape only: skip the leading `HeaderMark` run, then trim a trailing one. Both heading forms use the same `HeaderMark` node name, so that walk misreads the other two layouts: - setext (`title\n=====`) has a single mark — the underline, *after* the text. It was skipped as the opening mark and trimmed as the closing mark, leaving `cursor` past `end` and an empty range. - closed ATX (`## title ##`) puts the heading text in raw source rather than a child node, so both marks are adjacent siblings. The leading `while` consumed them both and pushed `cursor` to the node end. Either way `depth` and `position` stayed correct while `children` came out empty, so the damage surfaced in AST consumers rather than in the editor: unlabeled outline entries (an accessible-name failure), short word counts, and `exportHTML()` emitting `

`. Split the two forms apart instead of sharing one walk, and take a single node at each end rather than looping. `lezer-helpers` already maps `SetextHeading1/2` to a depth, so setext was meant to work — this restores the text to match.

fix(core): read link and image titles instead of hardcoding null

`title` was pinned to `null` on every Link and Image, even though Lezer
already exposes the title as a `LinkTitle` child. CommonMark permits three
delimiter forms — `"…"`, `'…'`, `(…)` — so read the child and strip whichever
pair it carries, collapsing an empty title to `null` the way remark does.

Destinations get the same treatment: the `<…>` form exists so a url can
contain spaces, and the brackets are delimiters rather than part of the url.

`adaptLinkReference` re-parsed the definition line with one regex,
`/^\[([^\]]+)\]:\s*(\S+)(?:\s+"([^"]*)")?/`, which lost three things the node
tree already had right — `\S+` truncated an angle-bracketed url at the first
space, only the double-quoted title form matched, and `identifier` kept the
author's casing where mdast case-folds it so `[Foo]` resolves against
`[foo]: …`. Read the `LinkLabel` / `URL` / `LinkTitle` children instead.

`live-preview-table.ts` already reads `node.title`, so it benefits directly.

fix(core): emit linkReference and imageReference for reference links

`[text][ref]`, `[text][]` and `[text]` all came out as `{type:"link"}` with
the whole raw source as the url, so `[full][ref]` exported as
`<a href="[full][ref]">` — a dead link — and the editor published the same
string as `data-link-url` while hiding none of the brackets, since the node
fell through to the GFM bare-URL branch.

mdast models these as separate node types: the destination stays in the
companion `definition`, and the reference carries `identifier` / `label` /
`referenceType` for the renderer to resolve. Classify the three forms off the
`LinkLabel` child and emit `linkReference`, with `imageReference` as the
`![alt][ref]` counterpart. `plugin-wordcount` already handled both types,
which is a good sign they were always the intended output.

The label walk that Link used moves into `readLinkLabelChildren` so
references share it and keep nested marks — `[**bold**][ref]` stays a Strong.

Changing the node type means the decoration path has to follow, or the
editor silently stops rendering reference links: `linkReference` joins the
`LivePreviewNode` union and the `isLivePreviewNode` allowlist, and
`getInlineMarkerStyle` gains a case that hides the brackets without
attaching a url it does not have.

One known deviation from remark, documented on `readReference`: CommonMark
demands a matching definition and falls back to literal text otherwise.
Checking that needs all definitions up front, turning this adapter's single
pass into two, and staying cheap enough for the live-preview hot path is why
it exists — so an undefined reference is still emitted as a `linkReference`.

files.patch:
@@ -25,6 +25,7 @@ function isLivePreviewNode(node: Content): node is LivePreviewNode {
     node.type === "html" ||
     node.type === "inlineCode" ||
     node.type === "link" ||
+    node.type === "linkReference" ||
     node.type === "strong" ||
     node.type === "table" ||
     node.type === "thematicBreak"
